title: Dual Lattice Conventions
body_html:
Dual Lattice Conventions

For a lattice \(L\) in a hermitian or skew-hermitian \(D\)-space with form \(h\), the unshifted hermitian dual is \[ L^\#=\{v\in V:h(v,L)\subseteq o_D\}. \] The shifted dual used in the Loke-Ma lattice-function normalization is \[ L^\vee=\{v\in V:h(v,L)\subseteq \mathbf p_D\}. \] Thus \(L^\vee\) is a one-uniformizer shift of \(L^\#\). Which side of the equality is written as a multiplication by a uniformizer depends on the right or left \(D\)-module convention and on the valuation normalization, so the knowledge base records the ideal condition rather than using an unqualified shift formula as a definition.

For a symplectic \(F\)-space \(W\) with additive character \(\psi\), the annihilator of a lattice \(A\subset W\) is a different construction: \[ A^{\perp_\psi}=\{w\in W:\psi(\langle w,a\rangle)=1\text{ for all }a\in A\}. \] This symplectic annihilator is not the hermitian dual \(A^\#\). In the knowledge base, \(L^\#\) is reserved for the hermitian \(o_D\)-dual, \(L^\vee\) for the \(\mathbf p_D\)-shifted hermitian dual, and \(L^{\perp_\psi}\) for the symplectic annihilator used in good-lattice finite quotients.
